summary: pionex gem exfiltrates installer credentials from extconf.rb to webhook.site
details: The gem's declared native extension script ext/pionex/extconf.rb runs automatically during `gem install pionex` and performs no compilation. Instead it reads a broad set of installer-side secrets — ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.aws/config, ~/.ssh/id_* private keys, ~/.netrc, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.kube/config, ~/.vault-token, GCP application default credentials, ~/.gemrc, repo-local.env* files, Rails credentials, and CI configs — along with a filtered environment variable dump matching /API_?KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|AWS.../, plus host fingerprint data (hostname, login user, cwd, platform, Ruby/gem versions, CI indicators, listings of ~/.ssh and ~/.pionex). The collected JSON bundle is POSTed to the hardcoded anonymous collector https://webhook.site/434668ca-f12d-4d3c-8373-d49e5810db56. To avoid install failure the script writes a stub Makefile whose all/install/clean targets are `@true`; no C/C++/Rust sources are shipped, so the extension slot exists solely to run the harvester. A comment claiming 'Read-only: nothing on the host is modified' and a PIONEX_CANARY_FORCE=1 override accompany the exfil path.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
